text:
I am very sorry about your situation and I hope you find a way out soon, with a positive outcome for you and the baby! From previous comments, I saw people recommend the Jerusalem Institute of Justice (Jerusalem Institute of Justice מכון ירושלים לצדק), who give free legal advice. I hope you can find help there.

I have not been in a situation like this, but I have been in a similar situation due to the Misrad Hapnim process. We, with my partner, applied for the partner's visa two times, one time when I was studying in Israel (6 years in the relationship) and one time when we returned from working abroad (11 years in the relationship). Both times I had to be jobless for around one year (one year the first time and 10 months the second time). The second time I realized how disturbing and highly damaging the situation is:

1. The foreign partner has no job and can become financially dependent.
2. The foreign partner has no social security, and due to the fact that one is forced to be in Israel while waiting for the visa, the partner cannot claim benefits from the country where they actually can get such benefits. In my case, I was able to get full social support from the country, which we left.
3. The couple together, the foreign partner and the Israeli partner, can go through increasing psychological pressure not only from Misrad Hapnim inactivity, but also because the family members can increasingly start questioning the choices made by the couple, blaming the couple for the situation and similar. For example, to my family, it sounds quite impossible that the government office can be so inefficient and make so many mistakes or simply provide misleading information that delays the process. As a result, some of my family members started questioning me rather than the process. 
4. Prolonged periods of being jobless is damaging to the career, and once the person gets the visa, it is not like they can instantly get a job. Psychologically, being jobless for a year and being unable to apply for jobs is highly disruptive to one's career. I can only imagine what it means when, in addition, the foreign partner has to be the only carer for their baby!

And the list goes on and on. Being trapped in psychological pressure, dependence and unsupportive relations, coupled with unprofessional and random situations with Misrad Hapnim, can make any functional relationship into a mess. Since we went through it two times with my partner, I started to speculate that it is not the process that takes a long time, it is all purposefully made for the partners to give up, break up or whatever. 

We are a regular couple, with no unusual components in our case; it is a straightforward case. And this second time we spent ~6000NIS only for flights, because the embassies abroad and Misrad Hapnim kept giving incomplete or misleading information to us. In total, the cost of documents, flights, and repetitive payments for the tourist visa, because of the constant delays in securing a date for the first appointment, cost us ~8000NIS. And again, regular case, no lawyer needed, nothing. This is nonsense.
